title: Throttling Starlink Is a Disaster for Ukraine and the United States
gist: Max Bergmann argues that throttled Ukrainian access to Starlink/Starshield, amid a breakdown in US-Ukraine ties, damages US credibility as a defense and tech supplier, risks European de-risking away from US firms, and threatens NATO trust.

themes.theme: Starlink throttling and the US-Ukraine rupture

insights.claim: After the US waived sanctions on Russian diesel and Ukraine struck Russian refineries, Starlink and Starshield service to Ukraine was disrupted, hampering interceptor drones against Russian jet-powered drones and front-line communications; the Trump administration denies restricting access and points to Elon Musk.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Single-provider dependence on a private satellite network is a strategic vulnerability for customers.

insights.claim: US leverage over Ukraine has shrunk because Europe now finances Ukraine and arms supply has diversified, leaving intelligence, satellite communications and Patriot defense as the last real levers.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Pulling these levers has high strategic cost to the US.

insights.claim: Starshield is paid via Foreign Military Sale and Starlink via a Poland-funded commercial contract, so throttling would be withholding a paid service and would read as the US defaulting on contractual obligations, making it an unreliable supplier.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Contract-reliability perception can hit US defense export and tech sales.

insights.claim: Europeans buy roughly 60 percent of their weapons imports from the US and Europe provides a significant share of US tech company profits, a tie that rests on trust in US security provision.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Exposure of US defense and tech revenue to European procurement shifts.
insights.quote: roughly 60 percent of their weapons imports

insights.claim: If services remain curtailed, Europe and other allies will de-risk from the United States rather than from China, developing less capable and costlier domestic alternatives that will erode US company profits, which Bergmann says is already happening.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Favors European defense and sovereign tech champions over US suppliers over time.
insights.quote: Instead of de-risking from China, Europe and other allies will de-risk from the United States
insights.locator: Perhaps it is not too late

insights.claim: Failing to restore the services would amount to the US taking a giant step to remove itself from NATO, since an alliance built on trust cannot survive extracting concessions from a desperate partner.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Tail risk to alliance cohesion and European defense spending.
insights.locator: Perhaps it is not too late
